newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait oil firm KPC 1997/98 net put at $2.22 bln.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait oil firm KPC 1997/98 net put at $2.22 bln.

text.p: A parliamentary committee has approved a 1997/98 budget for Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) with a projected net profit of 671.61 million dinars ($2.22 billion), a newspaper reported on Sunday.
The projected budget put revenues at 3.97 billion dinars and expenditure at 3.30 billion for the current fiscal year which started July 1, al-Rai al-Aam daily said.
It said the budget was approved by parliament's financial committee.

State-owned KPC, seen as one of the world's 10 largest oil firms, owns companies that produce, refine and market oil and petrochemicals and explore for oil and gas internationally and run an oil tanker business.
KPC last month reported a 1996/97 net profit of 870.8 million dinars on total revenues of 5.9 billion dinars.

Oil prices are currently some 30 percent lower than from the end of 1996 when oil exporters recorded higher than forecast revenues. Kuwait, which controls about 10 percent of world oil reserves, currently produces about two million barrels per day.
The tiny state has plans to raise production capacity by one million bpd early in the next century from a a current 2.5 million bpd.
